title: One word per worksheet line on 666,993 keyword tableaux: column key + a free letter per line, a speed per word, own speed and start per word, and a strip moved by the column key; 6 word-break parsings of the clues, column from word start or end, Vigenere / Beaufort / lines taking turns
k4_result: 0 of 873,760,568 exact tests pass (666,993 alphabets x 5 layouts = 3,334,964 key streams x 262 tests; every test has 9 to 21 checks and must pass all of them; chance predicts about 0.00001 passes). Nothing to decrypt. The most checks any failed test held before one broke is 6 (2 tests, both on ANTINEURITIC M/KRYPTOS); 401 tests held exactly 5. Without any dictionary: EAST is enciphered FLRV and GKSS, so one line letter between the two EASTs would put R and V on one place; that makes 68 of the 262 tests impossible for ANY pair of alphabets (hidden or not), among them the idea's headline case EAST|NORTH|EAST + BERLIN|CLOCK with key = a[line] + b[column] (14 checks) in Vigenere, in Beaufort, and with lines taking turns, column counted from either end.
controls: 11 shuffled K4s: 3 on a third of the alphabets each (plus A-Z and KRYPTOS) and 8 on all 666,993. 0 passes in all 11. Most checks held by a failed test: 5 or 6 in every one (6 in 4 of the 11). Tests that held exactly 5 checks, 8 full shuffles: 9, 43, 87, 31, 34, 19, 118, 62 against K4's 401. K4 is higher than all 8, and the cause was found: the key under NORTH (cipher QQPRN) is an evenly stepping run on 1,364 key streams against 312-627 for four shuffles (chance about 380), because plain N,O next to each other sit under the doubled Q; each such stream trips up to 32 of the tests that share those five checks. None of them goes on: streams where two or more clue words step evenly (other than NORTH inside NORTHEAST) number 10 for K4 against 4, 12, 25, 4 for shuffles.
planted: 6/6 among 33,350 decoy alphabets: column key UNDERGROUND + row word LANGLEY with EAST|NORTHEAST + BERLINCLOCK (11 checks, 63 of 73 outside letters read, 0 wrong, big model -4.38); column counted from the word end, Beaufort (14 checks, 54 right, 0 wrong, -4.42); a speed per word (19 checks, 55 right, 1 wrong, -4.49); lines taking turns Vigenere/Beaufort (14 checks, 57 right, 4 wrong, -4.50); strip moved by the column key (16 checks, 61 right, 0 wrong, -4.36); own speed and start per word (18 checks, 49 right, 6 wrong, -5.09). The true setting was found by the exact test every time and read best. It was NOT the single survivor: 1-5 neighbouring tests that the same key also satisfies passed too (a coarser word-break parsing, the more general own-speed model, and once the sister alphabet NULLIFIES for NULLIFIER); no decoy tableau of a different word passed.
scope_limits: Lines are single words; says nothing if the lines are sentences, phrases or a fixed number of words (only the two whole clue phrases as lines were also tried). Word breaks inside the clues: EAST|NORTH|EAST, EAST|NORTHEAST or EASTNORTHEAST with BERLIN|CLOCK or BERLINCLOCK. Tableaux: A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms (666,993), five layouts; the key is added mod 26 in the tableau's own numbering. Key rules: a[line] + b[column]; a[line] x column + b0 with the column counted from 0 or 1; a[line] x column + s[line]; K_i = K_(i-1) + d[column] with no line letter (with a line letter this is the first rule again). Not covered: a column key that also depends on the word length, a line letter that multiplies the column key, line letters tied to a rule (the row word is left free, so nothing was asked of it), two-letter steps per line, hidden alphabets (except the 68 tests killed by the EAST clash, which fall for any alphabets), a clue position off by one. The reader for survivors was only exercised on planted texts, since K4 and the shuffles gave none; it reads dictionary words of 3+ known letters and leaves short words as '?'.

negative.family: One word per line: column key plus line letter (ragged lines)
negative.hypothesis: K4 was enciphered from a worksheet with one plaintext word per line, the key letter set by the place inside the word plus a free letter (or a speed) for each line.
negative.scope: 666,993 keyword alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and both transposition-mixed forms) x 5 layouts; clue word breaks EAST|NORTH|EAST / EAST|NORTHEAST / EASTNORTHEAST with BERLIN|CLOCK / BERLINCLOCK; key = a[line] + b[column], a[line] x column + b0 (column from 0 or 1), a[line] x column + s[line], or the strip moved on by d[column] with no line letter; column counted from the word start or end; all lines Vigenere, all Beaufort, or taking turns; 262 exact tests of 9-21 checks per key stream, 873,760,568 tests.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 tests pass on K4 (chance 0.00001), most checks held by a failed test 6 (controls: 11 shuffled K4s, 8 of them on all alphabets, 0 passes, most checks held 5-6; planted 6/6 found and read back, 49-63 of 73 outside letters). 68 of the 262 tests, including EAST|NORTH|EAST as three lines with one column key and a line letter, are impossible for any alphabets at all because EAST is enciphered FLRV and GKSS.

follow_ups: The EAST clash as a general filter: any model in which the two EASTs (letters 22-25 and 31-34) get keys that differ by one constant is dead for every tableau, known or hidden, since FLRV -> GKSS would need R and V on one place. Run every family in kryptos/clues.py through this one-line test (key difference constant over the four letters) and mark those it kills; it needs no dictionary and no search.

Lines of a fixed number of words or of whole phrases (the thing this run does not cover): the unknown is where the line breaks fall before letter 22 and between the clues. For key = a[line] + b[column] with lines of 2-4 words, enumerate the column of the first clue letter in each block (0-20) and the breaks inside the clues; each choice is the same small exact system, about 21 x 21 x a few dozen layouts per key stream.

The key under NORTH (cipher QQPRN) steps evenly on 1,364 keyword key streams against about 380 by chance, because plain N,O sit under the doubled Q. A short check whether any of those 1,364 streams makes the WHOLE of EASTNORTHEAST or BERLINCLOCK a run with at most one break would close 'a progressive key with one slip' on these tableaux; idea 102 covered slips only for repeating and sliding keys.
